en_alt: He became lost in thought over the answer.
He thought hard about the answer.
note: "Fell into thought" is a marginal collocation; the alts give the drill the two renderings a native would write.

en_alt: I will think about this later.
I'll think about it later.
note: об э́том is equally "about this"; contraction variant helps the word-bank drill.

ru: В тако́й ситуа́ции она́ заду́малась бы о бу́дущем.
en: In such a situation she would start thinking about the future.
en_alt: In a situation like that she would start thinking about the future.
note: тако́й is "such/like this", not "that", and the inceptive заду́маться is lost in a bare "would think".

en_alt: Drop in on me after work.
Come round to my place after work.
note: ко мне is "to me/my place"; the alts avoid the added "to see".

ru: Я зашёл в магази́н за хле́бом.
Ты зайдёшь в магази́н за хле́бом?

en_alt: They will order a taxi for eight.
note: к во́семи is just "for eight"; the alt drops the added "o'clock".
Frame-only collision: the partner sentences are habitual present statements, so the imperative reading is unambiguous.

ru: Что бы вы заказа́ли на у́жин?
note: Menu-choice hypothetical; "would order" is the right reading of the perfective here.

ru: В кафе́ я зака́зываю ко́фе и торт.
note: Frame collision only: the partner is an imperative, so the habitual present is still distinguishable.
"on Fridays" already marks this as the habitual imperfective against the perfective imperative partner.

en_alt: They were finishing the building work in the summer.
note: стро́йка is the building work/site; alt keeps the drill from rejecting it.

ru: Всю неде́лю мы бу́дем зака́нчивать прое́кт.
note: Compound future correctly rendered "will be finishing".
Frame collision, but "at six" (habitual point) vs the partner's "by five" (deadline) leaves a usable cue.

ru: По пя́тницам она́ зака́нчивала бы рабо́ту ра́ньше.
note: Habitual "would finish" is exactly what the imperfective бы + past carries.

ru: Все уро́ки зака́нчиваются в два часа́.

en_alt: Our conversation would always end the same way.
note: Habitual "would" is an equally good reading of the imperfective past.

ru: В чём бы заключа́лась тогда́ цель?
en_alt: What would the goal consist of then?
What would the aim consist of then?
note: цель is glossed "goal", and the fronted "What then would…" is stilted; alts cover both.

en_alt: The problem lies in the money.
The problem is money.
note: Bare "lies in money" is thin English; the alts are what a native would write.

en: The difficulties lay in a lack of time.
en_alt: The difficulties consisted in a lack of time.
note: English "consist of" takes parts of a whole; заключа́ться в here is "lie in / consist in".

ru: На таки́х усло́виях мы не заключи́ли бы догово́р.
en: On such terms we would not conclude a contract.
en_alt: We would not sign a contract on such terms.
note: таки́х is "such", not "those", and "conclude a contract" matches the headword gloss while staying natural.

en_alt: The countries made peace.
note: заключи́ть мир is idiomatically "make peace"; keeps en_gb aligned with the gloss.

en_alt: I will conclude a deal with them.
I will strike a deal with them.
note: Alt matching the headword gloss "to conclude".

en_alt: Soon the parties will conclude a truce.
note: сто́роны in this sense is equally "the parties".

en_alt: We will sign the contract tomorrow.

ru: Она́ зако́нчила университе́т в про́шлом году́.
en_alt: She finished university last year.
note: "Graduated from" is the right idiom; the literal "finished university" is equally natural British English.

en_alt: Finish the work by five o'clock.
note: Frame collision with the imperfective imperative, but the deadline "by five" vs "at six" is a real cue; alt restores часа́м.

ru: Без э́тих поме́х она́ зако́нчила бы ра́ньше.
note: Perfective бы + past correctly rendered as a past counterfactual "would have finished".

ru: Я зако́нчил рабо́ту и пошёл домо́й.
Без де́нег прое́кт зако́нчился бы прова́лом.
note: Perfective counterfactual correctly "would have ended".

ru: Е́сли бы я испуга́лся, я бы закрича́л.
note: Past counterfactual with "would have shouted" — correct for the perfective.

en_alt: Soon the fans will cry out with delight.

en: They used to close the shutters against the sun.
en_alt: They would close the shutters against the sun.
note: Imperfective past read as a plain completed "closed", colliding with the perfective partner "She closed the book"; the habitual reading forces закрыва́ть.

ru: С за́втрашнего дня я бу́ду закрыва́ть магази́н ра́ньше.
note: Compound future correctly "I'll be closing".

ru: Вы закрыва́ли бы все о́кна на ночь?
note: Imperfective бы = habitual "would close"; correct.

en_alt: Close the windows at night.
note: Matches the rendering of на́ ночь in the sibling sentences.

ru: Вы закры́ли бы дверь на ключ?
note: закры́ть на ключ is exactly "to lock"; a word-for-word alt would not be English.

en_alt: I will close the window, it's cold here.
I'll close the window; it is cold here.

note: Perfective correctly a single completed event; the collision is fixed on the imperfective side.
Participle, not a finite verb — no real contrast-drill ambiguity.

ru: Е́сли бы он не бро́сил, он бы закури́л.
en: If he hadn't quit, he would have lit up.
en_alt: If he had not given up, he would have lit up.
note: The protasis is an explicit past counterfactual, so the perfective apodosis must be "would have lit up", not "would light up".

en_alt: He lit a cigarette in the street.
He lit up a cigarette outside.
note: на у́лице is "in the street" in British English.
Idiomatic and accurate rendering of заложи́ть закла́дкой.
«заложи́ть кирпичи́» reads oddly — заложи́ть takes an opening (заложи́ть прое́м кирпичо́м); plain bricklaying is укла́дывать/класть кирпичи́. Needs a native check.

ru: Где вы заложи́ли бы фунда́мент но́вого до́ма?
Э́ту дета́ль ма́стер замени́л бы сра́зу.
note: Present hypothetical; "part" and "technician" are the right senses of дета́ль and ма́стер here.

en_alt: Soon the mechanic will replace the oil.
note: "Change the oil" is the English idiom; the literal alt keeps the drill fair.

en_alt: He changed the wheel on the car.

ru: От стра́ха я бы замерла́ на ме́сте.
en_alt: Out of fear I would freeze on the spot.
note: "From fear" is slightly translationese; "out of fear" is the natural collocation.

ru: Ско́ро весь зал замрёт в ожида́нии.

note: ухо́д here is "departure"; the sentence is right even though the corpus gloss shows "care".

ru: При я́рком све́те она́ заме́тила бы оши́бку.
note: Perfective counterfactual correctly "would have noticed".

en_alt: She noticed every little thing.
She would notice every little detail.
note: Habitual imperfective; both the plain past and "would" readings are valid.

ru: Со вре́менем ты бу́дешь замеча́ть ме́лочи.
en_alt: With time you'll be noticing the little things.

ru: Мы не замеча́ем вре́мени за игро́й.
en_alt: We don't notice the time while we are playing.

ru: Без очко́в он не замеча́л бы э́той оши́бки.
note: Imperfective бы correctly a present counterfactual "would not notice".

en_alt: The children fell silent at once.
note: сра́зу is glossed "at once" corpus-wide.

ru: Ско́ро шум сти́хнет, и все замолча́т.
Е́сли бы я попроси́л, он бы замолча́л.
note: Perfective past counterfactual correctly "would have fallen silent".

en_alt: Stop talking, please!
Fall silent, please!
note: "Be quiet" is the idiomatic imperative; the alts give the literal reading.

ru: На её ме́сте я не занима́л бы де́нег у друзе́й.
note: English is right, but занима́ть "to borrow (money)" is a sense the headword gloss "to occupy" does not cover — the gloss looks like the half that needs widening.

en_alt: Are you taking my place?
Are you occupying my seat?
The books take up the whole shelf.

ru: Э́ти кни́ги бу́дут занима́ть всю по́лку.
en_alt: These books will take up the whole shelf.
note: "Will be occupying" is stilted with a stative verb; the alt is what a native would write while keeping the imperfective future.

ru: Будь бо́льше вре́мени, они́ занима́лись бы му́зыкой.

en_alt: Do sport every single day.
Play sport every day.

ru: С о́сени я бу́ду занима́ться пла́ванием.
en_alt: From autumn I'll be taking up swimming.
From the autumn I'll be doing swimming.
note: "Do swimming" is acceptable British usage for занима́ться пла́ванием; alts widen the drill.

en_alt: We studied the Russian language together.
Do you study music in the evenings?
Do you practise music in the evenings?
note: "Do music" is thin here; the alts match the headword gloss "to study".

en_alt: I study music in the evenings.
I practise music in the evenings.
I will take a seat by the window.
I will take a place by the window.
note: Russian has no article, so both readings are valid.

ru: Вы за́няли бы ме́сто у окна́ и́ли у две́ри?

en_alt: Soon the guests will take all the seats.

ru: Они́ за́няли все места́ в за́ле.
en_alt: They took all the seats in the hall.
Let's get to work.
Let's get down to it.
note: Idiom rendered idiomatically; alts cover the equally common English versions.

en: We'll get down to the renovation soon.
en_alt: We'll take on the renovation soon.
We'll start on the repairs soon.
note: "Take up the renovation" is not an English collocation; заня́ться + instrumental here is "get down to".

ru: По́сле экза́менов она́ заняла́сь бы спо́ртом.
note: Future-oriented hypothetical; "would take up" reads correctly.

ru: От бо́ли он бы заора́л на весь дом.
en: In pain he would start yelling for the whole house to hear.
en_alt: From the pain he would start yelling across the whole house.
note: "From pain" is translationese, and заора́ть is inceptive — the sibling sentence already renders на всю у́лицу as "for the whole street to hear".
